def: A rectangular table of numbers with a shape (rows, columns) that also acts as a linear function on vectors.
The vector whose entries are the dot products of each row of the matrix with the input vector.
A function that preserves addition and scaling, so that f(ax + by) = a f(x) + b f(y); every one is a matrix.
One of the standard unit vectors e1, e2, ...; the columns of a matrix are the images of these.
The product AB defined so that (AB)x = A(Bx): composition of linear maps, with entries given by row-column dot products.
The matrix with ones on its diagonal and zeros elsewhere, which leaves every vector unchanged.
The matrix with rows and columns swapped; it reverses the order of products, (AB)^T = B^T A^T.
The factor by which a square matrix scales areas or volumes; negative if it flips orientation and zero if it flattens space.
The matrix that undoes another, A^-1 A = I, which exists only when the determinant is non-zero.
A square matrix with no inverse because it flattens space and loses information.
The ratio of the largest to the smallest stretch of a matrix, measuring how much it amplifies errors when solving a system.
A group of examples stacked as the rows of a matrix so that one product processes them all.
The rule that (m, n) @ (n, p) gives (m, p): the inner sizes must agree and vanish.
